newsitem.title: UK: Gen Cable pays 16 mln stg for Imminus execs.
newsitem.headline: Gen Cable pays 16 mln stg for Imminus execs.

text.p: Four directors of UK managed data network services Imminus Ltd were on Thursday set to become millionaires as part of a golden handcuff deal by General Cable Plc, the cable operator that bought the group.

General Cable's chairman Sir Anthony Cleaver told a news conference that the company, which is paying a total of 33 million stg for Imminus, was giving the directors a total of 16 million pounds to stay with the company.
General Cable's finance director David Miller said it was the right acquistion, at the right time, for the right price.

Imminus, which made a pretax profit of 2.76 million stg in 1996 and was bought at 7.5 times historic EBIDTA (earnings before interest, depreciation, tax and amortisation), comes with a national licence.
This allows General Cable to offer its voice and data services to customers outside its regional franchise areas.

Imminus, which offers value added services enabling companies to link remote personal computers and terminals throughout the UK through its leased private network, will form part of General Telecommunications -- General Cable's new brand name for its telecoms services to business customers.
General Cable, which has completed 57 percent of its regional network, said it had no plans to become a national operator.

But managing director Philippe Galteau said that in order to be able to offer services to all corporate client sites, the group might consider building pockets of a new lines or leasing lines from other players.
"Interconnection charges are collapsing, there is an abundance of capacity and we can pick and chose," he told Reuters.
Earlier, the group reported wider annual pretax losses of 29.8 million stg against 21.17 million in 1995 after acquisitions.
General Cable also reported positive operating cash flow at 8.7 million stg, 42,900 new television customers, 40,700 new residential telephone customers and 12,500 new business lines.
